question: Can a small permutation-invariant neural network, supervised only to order adjacent microscopic hard-disk velocity sets in time, learn a scalar resembling the negative Boltzmann H-functional without being given its analytic form?

key_findings.claim: The physical target is a coarse-grained kinetic H-functional, not entropy of the full reversible microscopic state.
key_findings.evidence: The paper reviews H(t)=integral f(v,t)log f(v,t)dv and dH/dt<=0 for the Boltzmann equation, whose closure invokes molecular chaos. The learned model receives only the unordered particle velocities, omitting positions and correlations. Elastic hard-disk microdynamics conserve phase-space information and are time reversible, so any monotone learned scalar pertains to a reduced one-particle velocity description and the chosen nonequilibrium ensemble.

anchors.section: IV Machine Learning the H-theorem: velocity-set input

key_findings.claim: The data cover one highly constrained relaxation family: 1000 equal disks, identical initial speed, random positions/directions, fixed particle count and collision law.
key_findings.evidence: The simulator uses periodic unit area, radius 0.003, equal mass, elastic pair collisions, all particles initialized at speed 0.12 with random directions, frame rate 60 selected after collision-count saturation, 500 time frames, and 500 statistically independent runs. No alternative speed distribution, density, particle number, external force, or collision law enters training or evaluation.

anchors.section: Figure 3: equilibrium and empirical velocity histograms

key_findings.claim: Permutation invariance is built in through a DeepSets encoder with one global-context update and mean pooling.
key_findings.evidence: Each 2D velocity is encoded to 16 dimensions, the ensemble mean is concatenated with each particle representation, a shared residual/LayerNorm context map updates each item, and a final mean plus MLP produces one scalar. This is invariant to particle labels and scales linearly in N at inference for fixed hidden width.

key_findings.claim: The supervision supplies elapsed-time direction densely through adjacent ordered pairs; it is weak relative to H values but not unsupervised discovery.
key_findings.evidence: The same siamese model scores V_t and V_t+1, and the loss directly rewards the later state having larger standardized output. Batch standardization blocks the trivial scale-shrink solution and a softplus temperature tau=0.1 sharpens ordering. Thus every example carries the correct arrow-of-time label, and a monotone proxy for progress-to-equilibrium is sufficient without representing H.

key_findings.claim: Training shows a late transition in the ranking objective, but the paper does not establish a physical phase transition or unique learned law.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 shows loss and mean standardized adjacent increment changing sharply near epoch 60 during one 120-epoch Adam training recipe. There are no multi-seed transition-time distributions, optimizer/initialization controls, Hessian or representation analysis, or causal intervention connecting this event to discovery of H rather than optimization dynamics.

key_findings.claim: The evidence for learning H is four representative curves after a separate target-informed affine fit on every evaluated run.
key_findings.evidence: For each run n, coefficients a[n],b[n] minimize squared error between a h(V_t)+b and that run's histogram-estimated H_t over time. Figure 6 plots four selected runs after this same-run alignment. No aggregate held-out correlation, R-squared, RMSE, rank concordance, confidence interval, or single global calibration is reported.

key_findings.claim: The colder ranking temperature visually tracks the reference more smoothly, exposing material sensitivity to a single loss hyperparameter.
key_findings.evidence: Separate tau=0.1 and tau=1 models are affinely fit per run. Figure 6 shows tau=1 oscillating substantially near the late-time plateau, while tau=0.1 is smoother. This is a qualitative comparison of two trained models, not a systematic hyperparameter or seed study.

key_findings.claim: Neither conservation nor monotonicity is quantitatively validated on the learned scalar.
key_findings.evidence: The analytic pair-collision rule conserves energy and momentum, but the numerical study reports only collision-count stabilization and velocity histograms, not accumulated energy/momentum drift. For the learned scalar it reports training ranking loss and selected curves, not adjacent-order violation rate, worst violation, monotonicity under held-out runs, or robustness to simulation timestep/bin width.

key_findings.claim: The design lacks the direct reversal and shortcut controls needed to resolve Loschmidt's paradox empirically.
key_findings.evidence: The paper motivates the study with reversible collisions but never velocity-reverses an observed state and tests whether the learned arrow reverses, never pairs time-forward and exact time-reversed microtrajectories, never shuffles positions/correlations, and never matches states by simple dispersion or distance-to-final-frame statistics. The scalar could therefore learn a generic clock for this initialization family.

key_findings.claim: The paper provides no held-out split, regime generalization, or compute scaling, so the evidence cannot support a universal learned H-theorem.
key_findings.evidence: All 500 runs appear to contribute to the single model and no train/validation/test partition is stated. Methods report 120 epochs, Adam, learning rate, hidden width, and use of the Snellius supercomputer, but not batches, run allocation, seeds, wall time, accelerators, FLOPs, or scaling with particles/runs. Future work explicitly proposes broader initial conditions and collision laws, confirming they are untested.

method.core_idea: Learn a permutation-invariant progress coordinate for gas relaxation solely from temporal ordering of adjacent microscopic velocity sets, then compare that coordinate post hoc with the Boltzmann H-functional.
method.mechanism: Generate deterministic elastic hard-disk trajectories from a fixed nonequilibrium initialization family. Encode each velocity with a shared MLP, communicate the mean ensemble embedding back to each particle, mean-pool the updated set, and output one scalar. Train a siamese copy on adjacent frames with batch-standardized softplus ranking loss so later frames score higher; afterward independently affine-align the scalar to histogram-estimated H on each plotted run.
assumptions: Particle labels are physically irrelevant, so the desired scalar is permutation invariant.
Velocities alone contain enough information for the coarse one-particle relaxation coordinate despite omitted positions and correlations.
Adjacent temporal order across the fixed initialization family is sufficient supervision to prefer an H-like coordinate over other clocks.
The hard-disk discretization at frame rate 60 adequately captures collisions and numerical invariants.
Histogram bin size 0.005 provides a faithful reference estimate of H.
Per-run affine calibration is an acceptable measure of overlap with H.
The molecular-chaos/coarse-graining perspective, rather than fine-grained reversible entropy, is the relevant interpretation.
A single compact architecture/training recipe and tau comparison are representative without reported seed variation.

techniques.role: Produces reversible microscopic trajectories whose one-particle velocity distribution relaxes.
Builds particle-label-invariant scalars while allowing each velocity feature to depend on the ensemble mean.
Supplies the arrow-of-time label by comparing consecutive configurations with shared weights.
Prevents output-scale collapse and penalizes incorrectly ordered adjacent frames.
Computes a binned reference integral of f log f from velocities.
Maps the learned scalar's arbitrary scale/sign to each run's H curve for visual comparison.

evaluations.setting: 500 independent 1000-particle, 500-frame hard-disk relaxations from one fixed-speed random-direction initialization family
evaluations.metric: Batch-standardized adjacent ranking loss and mean normalized score increment over 120 epochs
evaluations.result: A sharp optimization transition appears near epoch 60 and settles to a lower ranking loss/higher positive increment
evaluations.baseline: Earlier training epochs; no shuffled-time, no-update, simple-clock, or alternate-architecture control

evaluations.setting: Four representative runs from the same simulation family
evaluations.metric: Visual overlap of separately per-run affine-fitted scalar with histogram-estimated H
evaluations.result: Tau=0.1 broadly follows the relaxation curve; tau=1 has stronger late-time oscillations
evaluations.baseline: Reference H after target-informed affine fitting and a second ranking temperature

evaluations.metric: Detected collision count versus frame rate, averaged over five runs
evaluations.result: Counts plateau near frame rate 60, which is then used for data generation
evaluations.baseline: Lower/higher frame rates; no numerical energy or momentum error analysis

evaluations.metric: Histograms with bin width 0.005 versus two-dimensional Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution
evaluations.result: Time-averaged/final velocity distributions visually approach the equilibrium reference
evaluations.baseline: Analytic Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at the energy-implied temperature

limitations: No train/validation/test split or held-out-run evaluation is specified.
The model is trained on only one initial-speed distribution, particle number, density, elastic law, box, and relaxation direction.
Per-run affine fitting uses the full target H curve from each displayed run, weakening the claim of independently discovering its quantitative form.
Only four representative aligned curves are shown; aggregate correlation, error, interval coverage, and monotonicity statistics are absent.
The learned scalar sees only velocities and therefore cannot represent position-velocity correlations or fine-grained microscopic information.
Adjacent order labels make time direction explicit; the study does not distinguish H from simpler progress-to-equilibrium proxies.
Exact reversed trajectories, velocity-reversal interventions, recurrence tests, and molecular-chaos violations are not evaluated.
Numerical energy and momentum conservation drift are not reported despite their importance to the entropy claim.
The H reference is histogram/bin dependent, with no bandwidth or finite-sample sensitivity study.
Only two loss temperatures and apparently one training run per model are reported.
Compute hardware is named but wall time, accelerator count, batch size, seeds, FLOPs, and data/particle scaling are omitted.
The evidence supports an H-like scalar for one coarse-grained relaxation ensemble, not a universal H-theorem or general thermodynamic law.
failure_modes: The network can learn elapsed relaxation progress, velocity isotropy, histogram smoothness, or distance to the common final distribution without learning f log f.
A velocity-reversed microstate may receive the same scalar even though its immediate trajectory runs toward lower coarse-grained entropy.
Per-run affine fits can make any strongly time-correlated scalar look H-like while hiding scale/slope instability across runs.
Batch standardization makes scores depend on batch composition and can obscure absolute comparability.
A different initial distribution, disk density, particle count, active collision, or external force may reverse or destroy the learned ordering.
Histogram discretization can induce apparent oscillations or monotonicity violations in the reference H.
Energy/momentum drift or missed collisions can masquerade as relaxation if numerical invariants are not audited.
Near equilibrium, adjacent states are almost exchangeable and the ranking loss can amplify noise-specific shortcuts.
Omitting positions prevents detection of correlations that invalidate molecular chaos while preserving the same velocity marginal.
A model selected after viewing H overlap may overfit the reference despite never using H in its gradient.
reusable_insights: For emergent-law discovery, distinguish supervision by time order from supervision by the candidate law; both can encode a strong arrow.
Require one global calibration learned on training regimes and frozen before held-out regime evaluation; avoid per-trajectory target fits.
Time-reversal pairs are the natural causal control for any learned arrow in microscopically reversible dynamics.
Compare learned scalars against simple clocks: moments, anisotropy, distance to equilibrium, collision count, and classifier logits.
Report monotonicity violations and invariant drift jointly; an entropy law is meaningful only relative to conserved quantities and coarse-graining.
Test position/correlation-preserving and velocity-marginal-matched interventions to locate what information the scalar uses.
Permutation invariance is an appropriate architectural prior for particle labels but does not itself impose thermodynamic structure.
Discovery language should be gated by transfer across initial ensembles, particle counts, collision laws, and exact reversals.
open_questions: Does a single global affine map from learned score to H generalize to held-out initial distributions, densities, particle counts, and collision laws?
What happens on exact time-reversed trajectories, Loschmidt velocity reversals, and recurrence-like segments?
Can simple statistics match the ranking and H correlation under equal capacity, data, and calibration?
Does including positions and pair correlations reveal when molecular chaos fails and the velocity-only scalar becomes invalid?
How stable are results across seeds, architectures, tau, batch composition, histogram bandwidth, timestep, and particle number?
Can the learned scalar satisfy a preregistered monotonicity violation bound while numerical energy and momentum remain conserved within tolerance?
Does a learned coordinate recover entropy-production rate or only state order?
Can counterfactual states with matched H but different correlations falsify the learned representation?

competitive_landscape.title: Machine learning the thermodynamic arrow of time
competitive_landscape.difference: Seif, Hafezi, and Jarzynski classify microscopic trajectories versus their time reversals, relate performance to nonequilibrium bounds, and inspect learned observables. The current paper learns a scalar from adjacent forward states of hard disks; it does not use exact reverse examples or test fluctuation-theorem calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep learning of thermodynamic laws from microscopic dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: Kuroyanagi and Yuge train pair ordering on molecular-dynamics snapshot images and test an induced order relation against adiabatic accessibility/thermodynamic axioms. Lier instead uses unordered velocity sets, a DeepSets context layer, and a shrink-resistant standardized loss, but evaluates only per-run affine overlap with H and fewer law-level tests.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning the Arrow of Time
competitive_landscape.difference: Rahaman et al. learn an arrow in Markov decision processes, connect it to reachability/side effects/intrinsic reward, and compare with a known stochastic-process arrow. The present work specializes the same ordering idea to permutation-invariant particle velocity sets and Boltzmann relaxation.

competitive_landscape.title: Using neural networks to accelerate the solution of the Boltzmann equation
competitive_landscape.difference: Xiao and Frank learn a collision-operator surrogate while enforcing conservation and the correct leading fluid limit. The H-theorem paper learns a descriptive scalar from simulation snapshots and neither approximates the collision dynamics nor builds conservation into the network.

competitive_landscape.title: RelaxNet: A structure-preserving neural network to approximate the Boltzmann collision operator
competitive_landscape.difference: RelaxNet/UBE proves positivity, conservation, invariance, and an H-theorem for a learned collision surrogate and tests in-/out-of-distribution flows. Lier's scalar is not a dynamics surrogate and has no structural guarantee; its distinct aim is extracting an order coordinate from raw microscopic velocities.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Sets
competitive_landscape.difference: Zaheer et al. characterize permutation-invariant set functions and introduce the sum/mean-pooling architecture. The present model adds a global-context equivariant update and temporal ranking, but permutation-invariant particle processing itself is established rather than novel.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine learning the arrow of time in solid-state spins
competitive_landscape.difference: Meng et al. use measured ten-qubit trajectories, forward/reversed processes, unsupervised clustering, supervised direction classification, and generative modeling of energy/entropy signatures. Lier uses classical simulated states and an order scalar; it lacks experimental noise and explicit reversed-process validation.

competitive_landscape.title: General H-theorem and entropies that violate the second law
competitive_landscape.difference: Gorban proves criteria for when convex divergences are Lyapunov functions for broad Markov kinetics and supplies counterexamples to universal entropy candidates. The learned scalar is tested on one relaxation family without a kinetic generator or universal monotonicity proof, so it cannot yet claim an H-theorem beyond that data support.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A compact permutation-invariant network, trained only on adjacent temporal ordering with a shrink-resistant loss, discovers an arrow-of-time scalar that resembles the Boltzmann H-functional in a reversible hard-disk gas.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The study combines an unordered velocity-set input, one global-context DeepSets update, standardized ranking, and a microscopic hard-disk relaxation; four aligned curves qualitatively follow H, and tau controls late-time smoothness.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The exact combination of velocity-set DeepSets and standardized adjacent ranking is a narrow implementation novelty relative to the inspected entropy/arrow work. Evidence does not establish discovery of the H-theorem: there is no held-out split, global calibration, reversal test, aggregate H error, invariant audit, shortcut baseline, or regime transfer, and the scalar is evaluated after per-run target fitting. The closest 2025 predecessor already learns thermodynamic ordering from microscopic snapshots with stronger law-level framing; the present contribution is therefore exploratory rather than a universal-law result.

reviewer_notes: Atomic full-text review of all 8 extracted pages, including equations, Table I, Figures 1-6, methods, and references. Figures 2-6 were visually inspected from the pinned PDF. Source is current arXiv:2508.14003v4 as checked 2026-08-23 (submitted 2025-08-19; most recently revised 2026-07-28), so this reading intentionally reflects the later v4 rather than the original 2025 submission. Anchors refer only to pages 1-8 of the extracted artifact. Eight distinct directly inspected primary arXiv competitors span learned arrows, learned thermodynamic order, set architectures, structure-preserving Boltzmann surrogates, current quantum experiments, and general H-theorem boundary results. Repository/code links are reproducibility context only and are not treated as evidence or forced mappings.
